findings.title: Update on a security incident involving 1Password's backend systems.
findings.summary_md: 1Password's advisory says investigation began on November 19, 2026, after signs that an attacker had gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account. The attacker used that account to read source code and push malicious code into backend services that downloaded administrative customer records, including names, email addresses, account and user identifiers, creation and last sign-in times, public keys, SRP parameters, and tokens in invitation and recovery emails. The company states that vault contents and the keys protecting them were not accessed, and that it disabled the account, revoked the stolen token, removed attacker-created access, and rotated potentially exposed internal credentials.

findings.title: Update on a security incident involving 1Password's backend systems. Customer vaults were not affected and all vault contents remain secure.
findings.summary_md: 1Password posted a community announcement at 5:33 PM UTC on November 25 saying no customer vault content or protecting keys were accessed and that services continued to operate normally. It described a limited amount of customer account information, including names and email addresses, taken from a subset of customers, and said independent cybersecurity experts had been engaged to validate containment and remediation. The post told customers no account action was required and warned about phishing attempts that reference invitations or account recovery.

findings.title: 1Password breached through an employee's GitHub account
findings.summary_md: Coding is Love reported that 1Password began investigating on November 19 after detecting signs of an employee GitHub account compromise, and that malicious code pushed through that account made backend services download customer account records. It notes the attacker copied private repository source code and entered the CI/CD system, which holds infrastructure secrets, and that the exposed subset included account and user IDs, sign-in times, public keys, SRP parameters, and tokens from invitation, provisioning, and recovery links. The article says 1Password did not disclose how many users were affected.

findings.title: 1Password breach leaked customer names and emails, but not passwords
findings.summary_md: The Verge reported that 1Password said a hacker stole customer names and email addresses after gaining access to its backend systems, and that passwords and other vault contents were not exposed. It said the breach could raise phishing risk, that the number of affected users was unclear, and that tokens from emailed invitation or recovery links had to be paired with single sign-on or a six-digit code sent to the user's email. The article notes 1Password lengthened those codes to 10 alphanumeric characters and added new detection for similar attacks.
